validation_policy.purpose: Show that the PR71-PR84 Product Delta package is internally coherent, lower-claim, reference-resolvable, and ready for explicit packaging later.

commands.name: all_package_json_parse
commands.command: jq . over all JSON artifacts listed in included_files plus the PR85 package manifest

commands.name: product_delta_boundary_lint
commands.command: python3 scripts/evals/lint_product_delta_evidence.py --paths over all PR71-PR84 Product Delta docs/JSON/review artifacts plus PR85 docs/JSON

commands.name: markdown_local_link_check
commands.command: Run a local Markdown link check over touched Markdown files.

commands.name: privacy_marker_scan
commands.command: Run the configured privacy/content marker scan over touched docs/JSON without embedding the marker literals in package artifacts.

commands.name: source_reference_resolution
commands.command: Resolve important source-ref paths and JSON pointers across PR81, PR83, and PR84 artifacts.

path_policy: All manifest files use relative paths only.
Source references should resolve to checked-in safe artifacts where the reference names a repository path.
Archive-relative identifiers are preserved as case identity only and are not treated as local archive-read permission.
important_refs_to_check: PR84 references to PR76 and PR83 artifacts.
PR83 references to PR81 packets, PR76 batch, and PR33 historical review context.
PR81 packet references to PR75 shells, PR76 broad reads, seed cases, and PR80 schemas.
PR75 and PR76 reviewed_artifacts and source_artifacts where present.

strongest_useful_signal.meaning: PR83 and PR84 preserved one downgrade from a broad positive PR76 read, making the evidence less impressive but more inspectable.

strongest_unresolved_risk.meaning: The PR83/PR84 real-case comparison is too thin and prior-positive to support product claims.

non_claims: The PR71-PR84 package does not prove Lolla improves decisions.
Codex-assisted reads are not human labels.
Specialist decomposition is not calibrated by this package.
PR83 and PR84 are not product proof.
Clean artifacts do not imply good advice.
Agents may not act on these outputs.
The package does not decide PR76 or PR83 is right.
The Product Delta eval lane is not part of runtime.
The package does not add judge calibration data, answer-quality scoring, automatic labels, or agent-use authorization.

notes: PR83 and PR84 real-case comparison only covers two cases.
Both cases came from prior-positive PR81/PR76 context.
No real-case no-change, added-noise, worse, or inconclusive outcome appears in the PR83/PR84 pair.
Checked-in safe mode uses compressed context and cannot fully test interpretation adequacy.
No raw transcript, raw revised answer, raw memo, or private archive content was read.
PR33 is used only as historical review-safe context, not fresh validation.
Future local-private mode may be needed to test interpretation adequacy more seriously.

next_decision_options.reason: The Product Delta Evidence phase now has enough scaffolding, boundary checks, package manifesting, and internal validation for explicit packaging.
Human review is the next meaningful source of stronger evidence, but it should be scheduled intentionally.
Raw context may be needed for serious interpretation adequacy testing, but it should stay local-private and outside checked-in artifacts.
Trap expansion may reduce optimistic review drift before a larger real-case batch.
A larger batch should wait until maintainers decide how to handle positive-selection risk and human-review routing.
